Subject: Priority lanes runbook & throughput contingency proposal — Novus Retail

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As promised I attached a lightweight operational runbook and a clarified SLA amendment that addresses the two items you flagged: guaranteed steady-state throughput for the reserved GPU pool, and predictable behavior when tenant isolation/queueing occurs during transient spikes.

High-level summary:
- Priority lanes: we propose a two-tier priority lane for your reserved pool — "Production" (lane A) and "Background" (lane B). Production requests get strict headroom and preemption protection during normal operations. Background is best-effort for batch/analytics.
- Throughput guarantees: steady-state throughput SLO is expressed as tokens/sec per reserved GPU with a 5th-percentile tail SLA for p95 latency on short prompts (<=256 tokens).
- Queueing behavior: during brief overcommit spikes we will shift new Background requests into a spill queue and maintain Production tail latency via burst tokens. If a sustained overload persists (>10 min), automatic fallback routes will shift Production to a compatible lower-cost model with the same API contract.

Attachments: novus_priority-lanes-runbook-v1.pdf (runbook), sla-amendment-redlines.docx (proposed contract language).

Next steps I suggest: 1) you review the runbook and redlines, 2) we run a short integration test with a 1-hour synthetic traffic run to validate burst behavior, 3) legal/proc begin redline review.

If you want I can loop in Ben (SRE liaison) and Lauren (contracts) — putting them on cc for visibility.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Looping in SRE + Contracts for proposed language and operational playbook notes. My quick takes after skimming Alex's reply:

- Escalation windows: agree we should make the mitigation ladder more granular. Proposal:
  * Tier 1 (0-10m): burst tokens + spill queue (no routing changes)
  * Tier 2 (10-60m): throttled Background and priority enforcement; begin pre-emptible instance provisioning (warm nodes)
  * Tier 3 (60m+): controlled fallback routing of Production -> fallback model (logging/billing parity preserved, see below)

- Billing / logging parity: Redwood can preserve token accounting by attaching a routing delta header and ensuring all fallback tokens show as billed against the original model SKU under a special "fallback" line item for reconciliation. We'll capture this as a redline in sla-amendment-redlines.docx.

- Production vs Background: suggest API flag x-priority: production|background or explicit per-route mapping in your ingress layer. Add runbook section with example cURL and SDK snippets.

Attachments: I updated the runbook with the three-tier ladder and an example cURL block. Attaching: novus_priority-lanes-runbook-v1.pdf (annotated).
